title: Nucleophilic addition of HCN
back: CN⁻ attacks the δ+ carbon (slow), tetrahedral alkoxide forms, then H⁺ gives the cyanohydrin. Aldehydes react faster than ketones.

title: Carboxylate resonance
back: Two equivalent structures; charge shared equally by two O atoms. That is why acids are stronger than phenols.

title: Rosenmund reduction
legend: BaSO₄ = poisons Pd so it stops at the aldehyde

title: Stephen reaction
back: Nitrile to aldehyde through an imine.

title: Etard and Gatterman–Koch
back: Two routes to benzaldehyde: from toluene (Etard) and from benzene (Gatterman–Koch).

title: Clemmensen and Wolff–Kishner
back: Both turn a carbonyl group into $\ce{CH2}$.

title: Cannizzaro reaction
back: Self oxidation–reduction: one molecule to the alcohol, one to the acid salt. Benzaldehyde does it too.

title: Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky
back: Halogenates the α-carbon of an acid that has an α-hydrogen.

title: Acid strength
legend: rule = more, stronger and closer electron-withdrawing groups make a stronger acid
back: Also $\ce{HCOOH}>\ce{CH3COOH}$; F > Cl > Br as substituents; 2-chloro > 3-chloro > 4-chloro.

title: Tollens' vs Fehling's
back: Benzaldehyde gives Tollens' but not Fehling's; ketones give neither. Iodoform needs $\ce{CH3CO-}$.

title: No α-H? Cannizzaro comes
back: Check for α-hydrogen before writing anything: dilute alkali aldol, concentrated alkali Cannizzaro.
